title: Kernel-image dimension formula and surjectivity criterion for algebraic groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $G,H$ be affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:G\to H$ be a homomorphism. Let $L=\ker f=G\times_{H,f,e_H}\operatorname{Spec}k$ be its scheme-theoretic kernel, and let $f=j\circ q$ be its homomorphism factorization [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization], with $q:G\to I$ faithfully flat and finitely presented and $j:I\hookrightarrow H$ a closed immersion. Thus $I$ is its closed image group scheme. Fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product]; closed immersions are [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], one has $\dim G=\dim I+\dim L$. If $H$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], then $f$ is faithfully flat if and only if $\dim G=\dim H+\dim L$. Here faithfully flat means flat and surjective on underlying spaces. All dimensions in these equalities are finite nonnegative integers. Neither $G$ nor $L$ is required to be smooth or connected, and no separability hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 5.23, printed p.104, and Remark 5.42 following Theorem 5.39, printed pp.108--109 (kernel-image dimension formula). The surjectivity criterion is its full-dimensional-image consequence, using Corollary 1.35, printed p.17, and the dimension drop for proper closed subsets of an irreducible algebraic variety. Used for the two homomorphisms in Lemma 16.39, printed p.338.

proof.text: Affine schemes are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], so the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] hold. Its specified factorization gives finite-type group schemes $I,L$, flat finitely presented $q:G\to I$, and $\ker q=L$. Every group scheme here is nonempty, since it has an identity section. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], all four schemes $G,H,I,L$ have finite dimension. Their dimensions are nonnegative because a nonempty space has a length-zero chain. The definitions [def-kun-dimension, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] give the same dimension, as both count chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets.

source.place: Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.42, printed p.108; finite-dimensionality input as in Proposition 5.23

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point] to $G\xrightarrow{q}I\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at the identity $e_G$, whose image is $e_I$. Both morphisms are locally of finite type, and $q$ is flat. The total fibres over the unique base point are $G,I$, and the fibre of $q$ over $e_I$ is $L$ with its identity point. The resulting equality is $\dim_{e_G}G=\dim_{e_L}L+\dim_{e_I}I$. All three identity sections are $k$-rational. For each of $G,L,I$, [lem-ag-rational-point-stalk-topological-local-dimension] equates this point-dimension with the dimension of its local ring, and [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension] equates that local-ring dimension with its global dimension. Thus $\dim G=\dim L+\dim I=\dim I+\dim L$. No smoothness or reducedness of $G,L,I$ was used.

source.place: Tag 02JS (lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive), equality for a flat first morphism; Milne Proposition 5.23 and Remark 5.42

proof.text: Now suppose $H$ is smooth and connected. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], its sole fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, namely $H$, is reduced after every separably closed extension of $k$; taking the trivial extension $k$ itself, which is separably closed because it is algebraically closed, $H$ is reduced. The affine-local smooth-ring characterization in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local] show that its local rings are regular. Apply [lem-wf-smooth-components-disjoint]: the irreducible components of the affine finite-type scheme $H$ are its connected components. Since $H$ is nonempty and connected, it is irreducible. Write $H=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The domain assertion of [lem-wf-affine-dimension-drop] shows that its finitely generated reduced coordinate algebra $A$ is a domain.

source.place: Tags 056S (lemma-smooth-regular) and 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal); Milne Corollary 1.35, printed p.17

proof.text: By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $j$ identifies $I$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq A$, and its underlying space with the closed subset $V(J)\subseteq H$. If $J\ne0$, the prime ideal $(0)$ of the domain $A$ does not contain $J$, so $V(J)$ is proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring], the topological Krull dimensions of $H=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and of $I\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$, which is homeomorphic to $V(J)$, are the Krull dimensions of the rings $A$ and $A/J$; the latter equals that of the coordinate algebra $A/\sqrt J$ of $V(J)$, which has the same prime ideals. The dimension-drop assertion of [lem-wf-affine-dimension-drop], stated for these prime-chain dimensions, therefore gives $\dim I=\dim V(J)\leq\dim H-1$. Hence $\dim I=\dim H$ forces $J=0$. Conversely $J=0$ makes $j$ an isomorphism and the dimensions equal. This argument does not require $I$ to be reduced.

source.place: Strict drop paragraph; affine closed-immersion description in Stacks Tag 01QO

proof.text: If $f$ is faithfully flat, it is surjective, so $f=j\circ q$ implies that $j$ is surjective. In the description $j:\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of [def-weil-closed-immersion], the prime $(0)$ must then contain $J$, giving $J=0$. Conversely, if $J=0$, $j$ is the isomorphism given by the quotient $A\to A/0$. The map $f=j\circ q$ is flat and surjective because $q$ is so by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization]: the isomorphism merely identifies the target points and local rings, so the flatness condition of [def-weil-flat-morphism] is identical. Therefore $f$ is faithfully flat if and only if $J=0$, equivalently if and only if $\dim I=\dim H$ by Step 4.

source.place: Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.42, printed p.108; elementary affine-coordinate consequence for a reduced irreducible target

proof.text: Using Step 2 and cancellation of the finite nonnegative integer $\dim L$, the equality $\dim G=\dim H+\dim L$ is equivalent to $\dim I=\dim H$. Step 5 identifies the latter condition with faithful flatness of $f$, proving both directions of the criterion.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 5.23 and Remark 5.42: Q32 assembles the dimension proof through the flat local dimension formula at the identity, Stacks Tag 02JS; the criterion uses the cited affine dimension-drop statement.
